brief: Garrett (GS FICC & Equities) frames the week's selloff as a violent positioning reset rather than a systemic event: volume and volatility data echoed COVID, the GFC, and 2025's Liberation Day, but Thursday's VIX stayed well below the 70+/60+/50+ peaks of 2020/2009/2025. SPX, NDX, and RTY posted among their largest 1-day-move-vs-implied-vol readings (a new metric Garrett calls MSR) in up to 19 years. Prime brokerage data show hedge funds net sold single names for an 8th straight week, US long/short net exposure fell to the 1st percentile, TMT long/short funds are flat on the year versus +24% in June, and the high-touch desk has sold $30bn of tech since the decline began, more than in July. CTA/systematic signals are now negative and modeled to keep selling SPX futures while buying bonds. Garrett's Vol Panic Index hit 9.57, a level that has historically marked a buying opportunity, and he recommends buying December upside call spreads in washed-out names (SOXX, SMH, EWY, XLK, URA). Separately, the desk likes shorting an overbought consumer-staples basket (GSXUSTAP) against cheap semiconductors.
